statement: The cover states an integrated system including ISO 9001 and Appendix B; this is declared alignment, not demonstrated compliance.
Quality responsibility extends across staff with a Q/EP/HS service and seven technical departments.
The organization identifies a testing laboratory; its test methods and results must be examined separately.
The organization identifies a calibration laboratory; this does not itself establish calibration traceability.
An independent emissions-verification unit is described; candidate; verify criterion mapping because independence is specific to emissions work.
If management does not appoint a quality/environment representative, the Q/EP/HS head takes that role and its authority.
The common manual describes the quality system and points to lower-level procedures; addenda hold system-specific requirements.
The Q/EP/HS head owns issue, application, distribution, changes and review of the manual.
The director approves the manual and each revision by signature.
Controlled manual copies are tracked on a distribution list, with numbered external paper copies and acknowledged receipt.
Revisions go to controlled-copy holders and obsolete copies are destroyed; uncontrolled copies require director consent.
The Q/EP/HS archive retains originals of both current and superseded manual revisions.
Staff access the current manual as a read-only intranet copy.
The reference list includes laboratory standards, Appendix B and NQA-1 but does not identify an NQA-1 edition or prove application.
The definitions assign company leadership to the director and department coordination to directors appointed by that director.
The supplier definition includes organizations or individuals providing studies, parts of studies, other items or services.
Control procedures are defined as written, approved methods for inspecting another party's activities.
Corrective action is defined as removing a nonconformance cause and preventing recurrence.
Qualified procedures are defined as proven fit for purpose under applicable regulations, standards and technical specifications; no qualification record is included.
Procurement documentation defines the requirements for acceptable goods/services and includes contracts, orders and specifications.
Nonconformance includes inadequate documentation and departures from requirements or procedures, not only faulty hardware.
Objective evidence is defined as verifiable information, records or facts from observation or testing.
The Q/EP/HS head appoints an engineer accountable for applying the systems to a designated activity.
QA is defined as planned, systematic action to establish confidence that specified quality requirements will be met.
Repair is distinguished from full restoration to the original specification; reliable and safe function can remain despite a specification departure.
General and task-specific quality procedures are written and approved, with task-specific documents supplementing common procedures.
Review is defined as a critical assessment against stated or expected requirements; the definition supports the design-review concept but not execution.
Rework is defined as processing nonconforming work so it meets specified requirements.
An audit is a documented assessment of adherence, adequacy and effective application of requirements and procedures.
Work instructions and procedures prescribe approved steps consistent with applicable rules, specifications and technical practice.
A specification includes requirements and the methods used to determine whether they are met.
Special processes are defined as needing control during work in addition to final control.
The manual treats design, analysis, consulting, testing and supervision as services within the product concept.
Verification explicitly includes checking supplier services against specified quality requirements.
The lead auditor definition requires experience/training to organize audits, report findings and assess corrective actions.
A record is defined as stating achieved results or evidencing performed actions.
Management, supported by Q/EP/HS, documents context assessment and feeds significant circumstances into risk consideration and possible action.
Contractor expectations include interdisciplinary consistency, reliability, safety and usable design outputs; candidate; verify criterion mapping.
Supplier expectations include guidance on quality-system requirements; candidate; verify criterion mapping to actual purchase flow-down.

The declared scope covers technical services including design, engineering, testing and measurements, incorporates nuclear QA and Part21 notification, and excludes accounting/legal/security functions rather than Appendix B criteria.
The manual names accredited testing/calibration laboratories and eLAB-PK with dedicated procedures; accreditation and test evidence are not demonstrated by this reference alone.
Nuclear work is stated to incorporate Appendix B/NQA-1 and Part21 reporting of nonconformances; detailed reportability and timing need their own evidence.
Important processes must be documented with their sequence, responsible roles, inputs/outputs, criteria and methods for execution and oversight.
The program requires resources, information, process monitoring and management evaluation of planned results.
Outsourced quality-affecting work remains subject to Ekonerg controls; oversight uses the design-supplier procedure or activity-specific plans/instructions.
The process table identifies responsibilities and interfaces; the table is examined separately rather than assumed from this reference.
Management commits to quality policy, implementation, oversight and resources.
Management periodically reviews quality policy and communicates it through the intranet/manual and other channels.
Quality objectives must be set at relevant functions and levels and be measurable where possible.
Important projects require quality plans; departmental plans are aligned and approved by management.
Management must preserve quality-system integrity during planned changes.
Management defines responsibilities and authority and publishes a director-signed organization chart to staff.
The designated representative or Q/EP/HS head manages system processes, reports improvement needs and coordinates internal/external quality communication.
Q/EP/HS works with process owners to identify risks; medium/high risks require treatment.
Planned risk treatments are followed by an effectiveness check, a supporting corrective-action principle rather than a completed CA record.
Plans for quality goals must state resources, responsible persons, deadlines and how achievement will be assessed.
Quality-system changes must account for their effect on existing authority and responsibilities and retain necessary resources.
Authors review unrevised quality-system documents for suitability at least every two years.
Management plans and provides resources for quality-system implementation and service requirements.
Personnel affecting product/service conformity must be competent through education, training, skills and experience, including applicable codes and QA duties.
The organization identifies competence needs, supplies training, develops awareness and assesses the effectiveness of those measures.
The program requires records of education, training, skills and experience; this is a retention obligation, not an employee training record.
PQ7.1-1 and project quality plans are identified as the routes for detailed competence/training requirements.
Management maintains infrastructure and plans necessary equipment, software and supporting services.
The work environment is to support effective work and conformity; no special storage conditions are proved by this general statement.
Measuring/test equipment must be identified, functional and checked/calibrated at stated intervals or before infrequent use; the stated commercial-equipment exemption must also be evaluated.
The manual exempts commercial equipment from calibration when it has the required precision; the basis and limits of that exemption need examination, not automatic acceptance.
Calibration results and equipment capability must be recorded; PQ7.5-6 is cited for control of calibration standards/documentation.
Equipment past calibration validity is specially marked and removed from use until recalibration; repeatedly out-of-calibration equipment is replaced or repaired.
Expired-calibration marking and exclusion provide a status control preventing unauthorized measurement use.
PQ7.1-2 and separate laboratory procedures govern uncalibrated, defective or damaged equipment; their detailed controls must be checked separately.
Departments/services maintain and periodically update knowledge lists using experience, errors, standards and training, including plans to close knowledge gaps.
Competence requirements are defined in procedures/plans, with departmental records of achieved competence.
Managers and Q/EP/HS provide awareness of quality goals, staff contribution and consequences of departures from requirements.
Internal quality communication uses director/department meetings, intranet information and direct management channels.
External communication includes required written reports and authorized contact with oversight bodies.
Quality procedures must give sufficient purpose, scope, responsibilities, application and documentation detail for consistent use and checking.

The hierarchy distinguishes common, project-specific, laboratory and verification-system procedures; project-specific procedures address personnel, equipment, methods, software and documentation when needed.
Work procedures must describe unambiguous steps and applicable prerequisites, resources, personnel, responsibilities, acceptance criteria and reporting forms.
Control procedures govern personnel overseeing work performed by other persons, departments or organizations.
PQ7.5-3 and PQ7.5-4 are identified for preparation, review, revision and format of control/work procedures.
Departmental work instructions require enough detail, acceptance criteria and team competence conditions for quality execution and checking.
Suppliers must demonstrate their work/products follow documented descriptions of quality-affecting activities.
PQ7.5-7 is named for identification, collection, storage, retention, disposition and maintenance of quality records.
The manual maintains procedure registers and a table of process sequence, interfaces and responsibility.
Document changes must be reviewed and approved by the same persons who reviewed and approved the preceding revision/original under PQ7.5-5.
External codes, standards, customer/supplier instructions and other necessary documents are subject to PQ7.5-6.
Document-control procedures assign preparation, review, approval and distribution responsibilities before use.
Review/update and reapproval precede use, with changes and the current issue status recorded.
Distribution is controlled and the current document version must be available where used.
Documents must be identifiable/readable, external copies controlled and obsolete documents withdrawn or distinctly marked.
Records provide proof of quality activities and must be classified, linked to product/process/service, readable, recognizable and accessible.
Linking records to the relevant product, service or process supports evidence traceability beyond mere document storage.
Inspection/test records must meet specific content needs and show acceptance criteria or requirements were satisfied; actual completed results are not supplied here.
PQ7.5-7 is referenced for protection, retention, accessibility, retrieval and lending of records.
Each work order/project has a team leader appointed by the responsible department director.
The leader plans project delivery, with documented quality planning for important projects and required work/schedule/inspection planning where applicable.
Project plans state staff numbers/qualifications and specific process, equipment, procedure and software needs.
The quality plan identifies verification stages, inspection and acceptance criteria together with relevant codes/standards.
The plan must identify applicable testing/validation needs and acceptance criteria; it is not itself a completed test report.
Quality plans define cooperation/communication interfaces with other groups, suppliers, customers and authorities.
Quality plans must identify the need and method for documenting quality records.
PQ8.1-2 and PQ8.1-1 link quality-plan preparation to graded activity complexity.
Customer communication covers requirements, contracting, requested verification access, post-delivery feedback and complaint resolution.
Department directors own customer communication and may delegate to project leaders; the director joins complex/strategic matters.
Product/service requirements include customer needs, unstated intended-use needs, legal/regulatory requirements and additional company requirements.
Before commitment, responsible project/contract/QA roles check completeness, resolve differences, confirm capability and document oral customer enquiries.
The project leader documents requirement changes and informs all affected parties.
Study/design work and supporting software are controlled from planning to verification; validation may occur when the customer uses the results.
Design planning defines stages, review/verification/validation, authority and group interfaces and is updated as work progresses.
PQ8.3-1 and PQ8.1-3 govern translation of customer requirements into design-planning documents.
Persons/services not directly involved in plan preparation independently verify its suitability under PQ8.1-2.
Design input records cover functions/performance, applicable rules, previous similar work and consequences of possible errors where applicable.
The design team documents detailed inputs and checks them for completeness, clarity and consistency sufficient for decisions and verification.
Quality/control plans define periodic checks of customer requirements and appropriate standards through completion of the study/design.
Design outputs must be verifiable against inputs, approved before issue, support downstream work, state/reference acceptance criteria and define safe-use characteristics.
Design records retain calculations/drawings/specifications/revisions plus key process steps and input sources supporting the final design.
Planned interstage reviews assess requirements and problems, include responsible designers and retain decisions/actions.
Completion requires planned internal analysis and verification by persons/groups not directly involved in producing the work.
Customer-requested external review includes the design team and produces retained verification records.
Later in-use validation is recognized; participating staff retain validation records and records received from the customer.
Before nuclear operation/use, physical and functional characteristics must be checked and documented against approved design requirements and the facility licence.
Design changes are identified, evaluated, verified and approved with original-work controls; competent approvers know the original purpose and requirements, and records are retained.
Purchased work/items must meet clearly defined requirements, with supplier oversight graded to their importance for Ekonerg delivery.
Procurement documents define work scope, technical requirements, tests, inspections and acceptance criteria with appropriate review and approval.
Procurement documents must state supplier-control methods, reporting, QA responsibility, access rights and nonconformance notification.
Department directors/project leaders own technical purchase requirements, supplier selection and verification of purchased work for their projects.
Supplier evaluation/selection and reassessment consider references, previous deliveries, other users, on-site nuclear audits and stated nuclear authorizations.
Supplier assessment occurs during tendering and identified shortcomings must be addressed before contracting; assessment/verification records are kept.
Purchase specifications include item/service details, approval needs, personnel qualifications, supplier QA, verification participation and required quality evidence.
Purchase specifications form part of supplier contracts/orders and other contractual instruments.
Purchased products/services are verified by testing or another suitable method; supplier-site methods and invitation duties are specified in purchase documents.
Supplier-site verification assesses QA evidence including incoming checks, work records, supplier evaluation and inspection/test documentation against acceptance criteria.
The verifier's written report accompanies completion/delivery documents as evidence of conformity before/after installation.
PQ8.2-2 is identified for issue, control and changes of procurement documents when Ekonerg buys work.
Controlled work requires product information, work instructions, suitable equipment, measuring/monitoring resources and delivery controls.
For normal services/products, quality plans and intermediate/final checks address defects that can be detected before use.
If processes whose defects are only detectable after use are employed, Ekonerg will validate and supervise them as special processes; this is a conditional commitment, not proof of execution.
Projects/studies and associated reports remain traceable through project work-order numbers and document-specific identifiers shown on the documents.
Records and documents associated with service delivery are maintained with work-order and document identifiers.
If customer property is used, it is to be identified and verified; retain the stated conditional scope.
If customer property is used, Ekonerg commits to careful handling, protection and security.
Damage/loss/unusable customer property triggers immediate customer notification and retained records.
Product preservation includes identification to the extent applicable to Ekonerg activities.
Applicable preservation measures cover identification, handling, storage, cleaning, packaging, protection and delivery/transport.
Preservation prevents damage, loss or quality degradation and must follow specific instructions/specifications or other developed documents.
Products with specified cleanliness, packaging, pressure, temperature or humidity conditions are specially marked and periodically checked.
Special handling tools/equipment and project-specific protection requirements include the handler's experience and training.
Post-delivery support includes stated document-retention obligations and customer feedback; actual retention periods require the detailed record controls.
Changes across studies, design and other services receive original-work review, competent authorization and retained change/action records.
Before delivery, authorized reviewers (or customers where applicable) document acceptance against requirements under quality/control plans.
Delivery review records must confirm acceptance criteria and endorsement by the persons responsible for release.
Nonconforming services/products are identified, marked, evaluated, dispositioned and controlled to prevent unintended use or delivery.
Nonconformities receive non-damaging marks and practical segregation; when separation is impractical, other misuse-prevention measures are required.
Disposition includes repair, authorized use-as-is with required customer agreement, repurposing, prevention of use, and inspection of reworked/repaired products.
Records retain the nonconformance, actions, approvals and customer agreements.
Repaired nonconforming work must be verified again to demonstrate compliance with requirements.
Post-delivery nonconformities require correction or action suited to their actual or potential effects.
Significant or repeated/similar nonconformities trigger corrective action including cause investigation.
The system plans monitoring, measurement and improvement with defined methods to check service conformity and program effectiveness.
Customer feedback and complaints are monitored/analysed under PQ8.2-1, supporting identification of adverse conditions.
Process monitoring defines steps, references, reporting, presence and performers; failure to achieve requirements triggers nonconformance and corrective-action processes.
Product/service checks follow procedures/plans and retained conformity evidence identifies the release approver.
Delivery requires completion and conformity; exceptions need director authorization and customer consent where applicable.
PQ8.6 is stated to define intermediate/final checks and independence of monitoring/measurement personnel.
The referenced control-plan process establishes witness and hold points (W and H).
When direct inspection is impossible or unsuitable, indirect control through the process, equipment and personnel is required.
The manual says Ekonerg does not test its own services/products; customer testing requires a program/procedures with test requirements, acceptance criteria and conditions.
For customer testing, procedures must define documentation and evaluation of results; the no-own-product-testing qualification remains part of the quote.
Laboratory service monitoring/measurement is assigned to dedicated laboratory procedures; their methods/results are not reproduced here.
Q/EP/HS and department directors analyse conformity, trends, supplier information and preventive opportunities and report to management in writing.
An annual internal audit program considers process importance/status and defines methods, scope, frequency and criteria with objective independent execution.
The manual requires qualified internal auditors who are independent of the area audited; no individual qualification certificate is shown.
Department/service heads address audit nonconformities and causes without unjustified delay; the lead auditor or QA head verifies action and reports to management.
PQ9.2 governs audit planning/reporting/records/follow-up; the same principles apply to nuclear supplier audits with trained auditors.
Management assesses system adequacy/effectiveness at least annually and records the assessment in writing.
Management review receives written audit, training, complaint, supplier, conformity, corrective-action, prior-follow-up and change information.
Written management decisions address process/product improvement, supplier issues, resources and personnel training.
Corrective action addresses causes and recurrence, evaluates proportionality, implements actions and checks success, with records and risk review.
The corrective-action sequence explicitly includes notifying the customer in nuclear work.
Significant quality actions are identified, documented, cause-investigated, tracked and verified for execution/effectiveness with status reports to appropriate management.
Quality policy requires staff application graded to activity importance and uses additional applicable nuclear standards where nuclear safety is affected.
Department/service heads and project leaders are appointed through defined authority; Q/EP/HS engineers are assigned as needed to activities.
Ekonerg retains responsibility for management-system work even when it delegates its development or implementation.
System personnel must have enough authority and organizational freedom to identify issues, secure solutions and confirm implementation, reporting to empowered management.
The director owns system establishment/application, manual approval, appointments, personnel qualification, resources, risk and management review.
Department heads own work and system application, plans/resources, competence and leader appointments; delegation does not remove accountability.
Project leaders own coordination, applicable system requirements and work/quality plans and retain accountability for delegated tasks.
The management representative reports system status directly to the director through reports and personal briefings.
The Q/EP/HS head is specifically responsible for periodic internal and supplier audits.
The Q/EP/HS head owns inclusion of system requirements in contractual and procurement documentation.
The Q/EP/HS head tracks regulatory changes and aligns system documentation.
The Q/EP/HS head owns generation, identification, collection, storage, maintenance and disposition of system records.
The Q/EP/HS head owns QA personnel training/certification, activity engineer assignments, process risks and reporting to the director.
The designated Q/EP/HS engineer works with the project leader but reports activity status/problems to the Q/EP/HS head.
Deputies have the same authority and duties as the role-holders they replace.
Employees are responsible for work quality, report nonconformities to superiors and propose corrections/improvements.
The process table assigns owners and interfaces for design, studies, tests, procurement, training and independent QA/control functions.
The QMS register identifies organization, risk, training and measurement-control procedures with revision entries.
The register lists document preparation/control procedures and their revisions; references are not proof of current controlled distribution.
The register identifies records control and project quality/planning procedures.
The register identifies supplier design control, procurement and supplier evaluation procedures; examine their supplied bodies separately.
The register identifies verification, audit, management-review and corrective-action procedures as the detailed system layer.
The manual register lists PQ10.2-2 revision 9; compare with the supplied procedure revision before asserting register currency.
The register names a turbine-testing control/verification procedure for NE Krsko; it does not include the test method or completed results.
A specific design-activity control procedure is listed for the national energy strategy work; this is a method reference, not a project result.
Prilog5 lists RVT visual-examination procedures for equipment, supports, welds and related items with revision/date entries; qualification and full procedures are not shown.
Prilog5 lists liquid-penetrant examination procedures including bearings; no process qualification evidence is contained in the list.
Prilog5 lists magnetic-particle examination procedures for bolts, pins and nuts; the list is not a completed examination record.
Prilog5 lists ultrasonic procedures for welds, fasteners, bearings, thickness and a specified instrument; full methods/qualification remain external references.
Thickness-measurement procedures name ultrasonic measuring equipment; calibration status is not established by a procedure list.
Coating-thickness, hardness and temperature measurement procedures list named instruments but no calibration results.
ROS02 covers use of the information system and ROS03 control of computer-program use according to the register; reconcile with software-check references elsewhere.
ROS04 is listed for backups and archiving network-server data; no backup execution record is supplied.
A system for equipment coding is listed, providing an identity-control lead without the coding procedure's full content.
The register lists study work, design-document production, QA in design, customer documents and design verification procedures; it is not a completed design-verification record.
RSP codes/titles in the register need comparison with nuclear-addendum references; preserve the differing source statements rather than correcting them silently.
Procedures for equipment testing/condition assessment and bearing assessment are listed; test acceptance details are not reproduced.
A water-turbine damage-repair method is listed; candidate; verify criterion mapping to controlled nonconforming work.
Quality supervision, incoming inspection and dimensional-inspection methods appear in the procedure register.
Control procedures are listed for NEK overhaul work on diesels, pumps, compressors, valves and HVAC; procedure titles are not completed inspection results.
Pressure-test control procedures are listed for pressure equipment and main pipelines; the methods and test records need separate support.
The nuclear addendum locates authority and independent-verifier requirements in the main manual and PQ5.3; details are not inferred from the reference alone.
Internal reviewers, project leaders and designers are selected from competency lists maintained by the design department director under RSP02 criteria.
NS, AQ and Large nuclear modifications must be graded at highest complexity level I; NNS work may be I or II depending on complexity.
NS design verification is assigned to RSP06 while other verification uses RSP02; full procedures are not supplied by this sentence.
The addendum points to internal design certification and nuclear lead-auditor competence provisions, not actual personnel certificates.
Nuclear design-input/customer-document control is assigned to RSP04/RSP05, with QA document control assigned to RSP03; compare the procedure register for code consistency.
For commercial products intended for nuclear safety-related use, dedication is documented starting with safety significance, critical characteristics and choice of verification method.
Design specification of commercial products for nuclear safety service includes identifying safety effects and critical characteristics before acceptance-method selection.
Nuclear design changes and departures must be identified, analysed, documented and approved by the original approver and customer where needed using original-document controls.
Minor commercial designation/condition changes are exempted from the original level of review/approval; applicability and safe limits of this exemption need evaluation.
The nuclear addendum explicitly maps procurement-document control to main chapter8.4; the body's specific controls are collected separately.
Q/EP/HS controls work/control procedure distribution, while the issuing department controls its work-instruction distribution.
RU02.1 is identified for drawings, specifications and other design-document parts under RSP02; its actual contents are not included.
Nuclear document control is mapped to main chapter7.5, whose substantive controls are extracted separately.
The nuclear addendum maps supplier assessment, offer evaluation, supplier documents, acceptance and nonconformities to chapters8.4/8.7 and PQ10.2-1.

Nuclear identification/status marking is to be addressed when needed in a specific document defining traceability method, special requirements and marking authority; such a project document is not shown here.
Nuclear special-process control points directly to main8.5.2, which contains the conditional validation/supervision commitment.
The nuclear addendum calls for a control plan at the stated quality level and names activity-specific/PQ8.6/RUK01/RDK01 inspection methods.
The nuclear testing clause points to main9.1.4 and software supervision to ROS02; the actual internal test-program text is collected separately.
The nuclear addendum explicitly applies main7.1.5 equipment controls; preserve the commercial-calibration exception for later assessment.
The nuclear addendum maps handling, storage, packaging and dispatch to substantive preservation controls in main8.5.5.

Nuclear inspection/test/operating status marking is to be defined as needed in a specific document covering method, traceability requirements and marking authority; current implementation is not established by this conditional commitment.
Nuclear nonconformance handling under Part21 includes identification, separation, removal, evaluation, disposition, resolution and documentation under PQ10.2-1.
Both Ekonerg and its suppliers are required to notify the customer of nuclear nonconformances; detailed reporting thresholds/timelines are not stated here.
Nuclear corrective-action initiation is mapped to main10.2; its cause/effectiveness controls are extracted separately.
Projects/studies are stored in a central archive and on a server, with a separate-location parallel server and hard-disk copies for protection.
The nuclear records clause cites RSP03 for data protection, while Prilog5 lists ROS04 for backups; the reference mismatch requires verification.
Nuclear audits are mapped to main9.2 and PQ9.2/PQ8.4-3, not to a claim of completed audits.
Nuclear level-I suppliers (NS/AQ/L) require a pre-engagement audit, except already nuclear-qualified listed suppliers receiving periodic audits at least every three years.
The exemption from a project-specific supplier audit depends on existing nuclear qualification and a continuing periodic-audit basis; it is not a blanket supplier exemption.

Level-I work requires verification of program results during use; other levels require pre-use verification on installation, upgrades/patches, OS/hardware changes, new users, two-year non-use or other verifier-defined conditions.
Software verification is tied to configuration and use changes, including programs, operating systems, hardware and personnel, supporting controlled design tools.
The QA-flow notes repeat NS verification via RSP06 versus other review via RSP02; this corroborates routing but supplies no completed verification.
The AppendixB crosswalk points Test Control to8.1.4 whereas the substantive nuclear clause points to9.1.4; retain this possible cross-reference error.
The environmental system explicitly reuses modified common quality procedures, supporting integrated-system reach without proving nuclear application of every environmental rule.
Environmental outsourcing uses PQ8.4-1 or activity-specific oversight; this corroborates a shared supplier-control mechanism, scoped to environmental work.
Design work incorporates environmental-study, elaborat or permit measures as applicable; this is a concrete example of external design-input flow, not nuclear design qualification.
Environmental regulatory updates are supplied daily and assigned personnel track them, with compliance checked during internal audits; nuclear rule monitoring is not proved by this scoped example.
Environmental competence evidence uses shared PQ7.1-1 for persons working for/on behalf of Ekonerg; supports the reach of common training controls.
Environmental document control includes current copies at use and a method for checking documents are used as intended; retain the stated environmental scope.
Environmental suppliers are informed/trained and supervised, and sign acknowledgement of system requirements and consequences under PQ8.4-2.
Environmental emergency procedures are reviewed at least annually and after incidents; this supports document feedback practice, not nuclear emergency preparedness compliance.
Environmental monitoring equipment is tied to shared PQ7.1-2 equipment control; calibration evidence is not included.
The environmental addendum applies cause-removal, recurrence prevention and effectiveness checks through the same PQ10.2 controls; this corroborates integrated use, not a completed action.
The occupational-safety section protects workers reporting incidents/hazards; candidate; verify criterion mapping because it does not expressly define nuclear QA concern protection.
Occupational-safety risk assessment precedes organization/process changes; candidate; verify criterion mapping to quality-affecting design changes.
The safety system maintains a separately updated applicable-rule list on the intranet and assigns daily regulatory-change monitoring; retain safety-system scope.
Safety programs assign action owners/deadlines and QA assesses effectiveness in annual reporting; candidate; verify criterion mapping to nuclear quality actions.
Safety competence documentation uses common PQ7.1-1, corroborating organization-wide use of the training process.
Staff are encouraged to report incidents and avoid serious life/health hazards without fear of consequences; this is not an explicit nuclear quality stop-work authorization.
The safety addendum specifies documented work responsibility, current instructions, evidence records, suitable equipment and competent personnel; retain its safety-risk context.
Joint-delivery arrangements define interfaces among contractors in a project manual, plan/program or other applicable document.
Changes in location, organization, equipment, regulation or technology require revised/new safety plans; supports a scoped change-control mechanism.
Health/safety requirements flow into procurement under PQ8.4-2, with PQ8.4-3 supplier evaluation and signed acknowledgements after information/training.
Safety monitoring equipment also uses PQ7.1-2, corroborating a shared procedure without demonstrating calibration results.
Safety management review considers prior actions, audit results, incident causes and corrective-action status before issuing written improvement decisions.
The safety-addendum register lists PQ5.3 revision7 while the main register lists revision8; this is a specific document-currency lead.
